claims.statement: SUPPORTED_MODELS is the curated selectable-model catalogue: each ModelOption defines a provider-prefixed id, label, allowed efforts, default effort, image capability, and optional default eligibility; SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS is the membership set used to validate selections, so effort and image support are model-specific rather than global.

default_model_pair is the deployment-level terminal fallback: it reads LLM_MODEL_ID and LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, requires a supported default-eligible model and compatible effort, and raises ValueError instead of constructing an invalid configured pair.

Unsupported non-deprecated stored model ids can recover to a same-provider pair, preferring the same Claude family and preserving a compatible effort; deprecated ids are excluded from that recovery path and DEPRECATED_MODEL_REPLACEMENTS currently contains no canonical replacements.

Workspace settings resolve in tiers of hardcoded defaults, non-null instance values in ['team_settings']/default, and non-null workspace overrides in ['workspace_settings']/slug; reads deliberately fail soft to hardcoded defaults when the Store cannot be read.

Workspace default model resolution guarantees a valid pair by accepting a supported non-Fable pair, otherwise trying same-provider recovery, then falling back to default_model_pair; review chat inherits the agent default when no valid chat-specific pair is configured.

Profiles are stored by login in ['profiles'] and contain main/subagent model choices plus repository, branch, PR, and feature preferences, while encrypted OAuth tokens live separately in ['oauth_tokens'] so concurrent profile and token writes cannot clobber each other.

Run-start profile lookup is fail-soft: load_profile logs and returns None on Store failure, whereas dashboard profile reads use get_profile directly; valid profile pairs override only when normalized as supported, default-eligible, and effort-compatible, with same-provider recovery for a stale non-deprecated id.

Thread agent_settings is a typed metadata snapshot with model, subagent, routing, handoff, and repository-instruction fields; it is cached for five minutes, malformed data becomes an empty snapshot, and normal persistence failures are logged without aborting a run.

The agent factory seeds workspace defaults, applies a profile only when a thread has no saved model or dashboard auto selection was reset, then honors the saved thread snapshot; a valid explicit agent_model_id/agent_effort replaces main and subagent pairs and the resolved settings are persisted before construction.

Adaptive routing is separate from the pinned thread choice: a profile routing boolean overrides the workspace toggle, routing stores tier pairs, and middleware-selected route attribution updates resolved_agent_model_id/resolved_agent_effort and run metadata for the turn.

In dashboard auto mode, opening-task model requests are classified against only available model options and valid efforts, rejected when unavailable or incompatible, and strictly persisted as a completed handoff; a successful requested model disables routing and is reused on later turns.

Fable models are workspace-gated: disabled Fable selections are substituted with a safe non-Fable Anthropic pair, workspace saves normalize Fable defaults when the toggle is off, and the options endpoint and factory apply the gate before advertising or constructing models.

provider_model_kwargs maps a resolved effort to provider-specific arguments for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini 3, Fireworks, and Baseten; make_model adds six retries and a 600-second timeout, configures OpenAI Responses behavior, supports desktop OAuth without an API key, and requires BASETEN_API_KEY for direct Baseten calls.

Gateway routing is tri-state: an explicit workspace boolean wins and None inherits LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_ENABLED or the dedicated gateway-key default; supported provider calls receive gateway base URL, key, and OpenAI Responses overrides, while missing credentials or unsupported providers are logged and left direct.

Runtime provider fallback is separate from setting recovery: the factory prefers LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID, otherwise maps Anthropic to OpenAI and OpenAI to Anthropic; ModelFallbackMiddleware alternates primary and fallback on retryable failures and surfaces provider-access errors to the user.

Prompt resources are loaded only from relative .md or .md.jinja files beneath openswe/resources/prompts, rendered with Jinja StrictUndefined, and can supply tool descriptions; invalid absolute or traversal resource paths are rejected.

Repository custom instructions are repository-access-controlled records in ['agent_instructions'] keyed by owner/name; the factory resolves them for a new thread's prompt repository, snapshots them in agent_settings, and renders them as mandatory system-prompt instructions that yield to AGENTS.md.

Personal instructions are capped, login-keyed records in ['user_instructions'] kept outside profiles so dashboard and agent-tool writers do not clobber each other; each prepare phase reloads participant data and injects a dynamic person context whose standing_instructions belong to that participant rather than a shared thread policy.

The main system prompt composes deployment prompt, source and environment guidance, repository custom instructions, and workspace instructions; the templates state that AGENTS.md overrides repository instructions, which in turn override workspace instructions, while structured user-controlled values are treated as data.
